p1.original: 14. 1创伤性事件、长期的生活状况、生活中的重大变化，甚至是小麻烦，都会引起应激反应。
p1.en: 14. 1 Traumatic events, long-term living conditions, significant changes in life, and even minor problems, can trigger stress.

p2.original: 14.2 身体的应激反应始于唤醒，唤醒会激发一系列生理反应。这些反应在短期内具有适应性，但如果持续时间过长，就会给个体带来伤害。
p2.en: 14.2 The physical stress begins with a wake-up call that triggers a series of physiological reactions. These responses are adaptive in the short term, but if they last too long, they can harm individuals.

p3.original: 14.3 人格特征影响个体对应激情境的反应，从而影响其暴露于潜在的应激源时所感到的痛苦程度。
p3.en: 14.3 Personal characteristics affect the individual's response to passions, and thus the degree of suffering that he or she feels when exposed to potential stressors.

p4.original: 14.4 有效的应对策略能减少应激对健康的消极影响，而选择积极的生活方式则会促进人的身心健康和提升整体幸福感。
p4.en: 14.4 Effective coping strategies can reduce the negative health impact of stress, while positive lifestyle choices promote physical and mental health and overall well-being.

p5.original: 2001年9月11日早上8：46，在纽约一家诊所外，退休消防员丹尼斯·史密斯（Dennis Smith）正等待一年一度的体检。这时冲进来一名护士，她说一架飞机刚刚撞上了曼哈顿世界贸易中心的北塔（Smith，2003b）。纽约消防局（New York's Fire Department，FDNY）的消防车和云梯车队已经响应了警报。消防车立即赶往事发现场，消防队员们冲进大厦，而大厦里成群的人正拼命地想要逃离。史密斯问自己，战友们面临着什么样的情境：在熊熊燃烧的大火中寻找通往大厦的最佳通道，查看楼梯井是否完好。被困在大厦里并面临死亡的人有多少？
p5.en: On 11 September 2001 at 8.46 a.m., outside a New York clinic, retired firefighter Dennis Smith was awaiting an annual medical examination. At that time, she came in with a nurse who said that an aircraft had just hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center in Manhattan (Smith, 2003b). The fire trucks and ladders of the New York Fire Department have responded to the alarm. The fire trucks immediately proceeded to the scene of the incident, and the firefighters stormed into the building, where a crowd of people were desperate to escape. Smith asked himself what the situation faced by his comrades was: to find the best way to reach the building in the fire that had burned, to see if the stairwell was intact. How many people are trapped in the building and facing death?

p6.original: 一名消防员事后这样描述当时混乱的场面：“简直就像电影中的画面，怪物来了，碎片像雨点一样砸向我们，各种东西在你的头顶上噼里啪啦作响。”（Smith，2003b）当他爬上北塔高处时，第二架飞机撞上了南塔，他回忆道：“突然，头顶上传来一声巨响。”他蜷缩在楼道里，清点自己的工具：“当时我在想自己的处境——应该做什么，还能做什么，有什么有利的条件，有哪些工具。头盔是我当时手中最重要的一件东西。我记得当时自己的想法是，戴上那顶头盔有多么的重要。”
p6.en: A fireman later described the scene of chaos as follows: "It's like a picture in a movie, the monster comes, the pieces come to us like rain, and all kinds of things snap on your head. When he climbed up the north tower, the second plane hit the south tower, and he remembered, “Suddenly, there was a loud sound coming from the top of his head. “I was thinking about my situation — what to do, what to do, what to do, what to do, what to do, what to do, what to do. The helmet was the most important thing I had in my hands. I remember my own thoughts about how important it was to wear that helmet.

p7.original: 但史密斯的战友迈克尔·贾奇神父却在关键时刻忘记了头盔的重要性，这听上去有些讽刺。他是消防局的牧师，也是第一批到达事发现场的人之一。在听说有消防员被困在大厦里后，他冲了进去。在进行临终告别仪式时，出于尊敬，他习惯性地摘下了头盔，就在这时，碎石和瓦砾从天而降，导致他当场死亡（Downey，2004）。
p7.en: But Father Michael Jatch, Smith's comrade, forgot at a critical time about the importance of the helmet, which sounds ironic. He was a pastor of the fire department and one of the first to arrive at the scene. After hearing that a fireman was trapped in the building, he stormed in. During the final farewell ceremony, he used to remove his helmets out of respect, as he fell from the sky, causing him to die on the spot (Downey, 2004).

p9.original: 在恐怖袭击发生后的几周乃至几个月里，消防队员继续搜寻尸体。他们埋葬、纪念和哀悼他们的战友。343名消防人员遇难。活下来的人眼睁睁地看着其他人就在几米远的地方死去，作为幸存者，他们忍受着内疚和矛盾的心情，不确定为什么自己值得活着，并且不断地问自己“为什么是我活了下来”。一些人出现了创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的症状，一次又一次地回想灾难发生时的恐怖情形。“9·11”事件的余波不仅影响了那些亲身经历灾难的人，还影响着世界各地数百万人，他们在数日里目不转睛地盯着电视，反复观看双子塔倒塌的情景，聆听幸存者对现场的描述（我们稍后会提到媒体往往是中介应激的来源）。
p9.en: In the weeks and months following the terrorist attack, firefighters continued to search for bodies. They bury, remember and mourn their comrades. 343 firefighters were killed. Those who survived watched others die a few metres away, and as survivors they endured guilt and contradictions, were not sure why they deserved to live and kept asking themselves “why I survived”. Some have experienced symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), reminiscent of the horrors of the disaster. The aftermath of the events of 11 September affected not only those who experienced the disaster first-hand, but also millions of people around the world who watched television for days, watched repeatedly the collapse of the Twin Towers, and listened to survivors' accounts of the scene (and we will mention later that the media are often the source of media stress).

p10.original: 幸存的消防员仍深陷悲伤中。许多人在回忆他们的战友时，不愿表达虚假的尊敬或忧伤，反而更喜欢拿逝者的怪癖和犯过的错开玩笑。曼哈顿第40消防车队和第35云梯车队损失了12名消防员，比其他任何消防站损失的人都多。和其他人一样，他们想知道失踪的受害者到底经历了什么。在“9·11”事件发生5个月后，他们看到了一段新闻视频。视频显示，在大楼倒塌前的几分钟，失踪的12名战友进入了双子塔。虽然这段视频是从远处拍摄的，但通过移动的身影可以辨认出是他们的战友。幸存的消防员聚精会神地盯着屏幕，看着那些再也回不来的战友。他们一遍又一遍地播放这段视频（Halberstam，2002）。
p10.en: Survivors of firefighters are still in mourning. Many, while recalling their comrades, do not want to express false respect or sorrow, but rather prefer to make jokes about the eccentricity and mistakes of the dead. The 40th Manhattan fire convoy and the 35th ladder convoy lost 12 firefighters, more than any other fire station. Like others, they want to know what happened to the victims of disappearances. Five months after the events of 11 September, they saw a news video. The video shows 12 missing comrades entering the Twin Towers a few minutes before the building collapsed. Although the video was taken from a distance, it was identified by moving images as their comrades. Survivors of firefighters will stare at the screen with their eyes closed to those who will never return. They played the video over and over again (Halberstam, 2002).

p11.original: 与其他大多数公务员不同，消防员大部分时间都住在消防站里。由于火灾和其他紧急情况相对较少发生，他们会在一起度过很多时光，一起玩扑克或其他游戏，以及看书、看电视。在大多数消防站里，家庭氛围会逐渐形成，当你明白这一点，便更能理解他们承受的是许多朝夕相处的“家人”突然逝世带来的巨大压力。此外，每个人都觉得自己有义务参加尽可能多的追悼会，不仅包括逝去战友的追悼会，还包括在培训新消防员训练中认识的其他消防员或者来自其他消防站中曾经一同工作的消防员的追悼会。对有些消防员而言，参加这些令人心痛的追悼会是一种持续一年多的折磨，给他们再次带来了无尽的痛苦。
p11.en: Unlike most other civil servants, firefighters spend most of their time in fire stations. Because fire and other emergencies are relatively rare, they spend a lot of time together, playing poker or other games, and reading books and watching television. In most fire stations, the family atmosphere will gradually develop, and when you understand this, it will be better to understand that they are under the enormous strain of the sudden death of many “family” who are living together in the morning and evening. In addition, everyone feels obliged to attend as many memorials as possible, not only of the deceased comrades, but also of other firefighters who are known in the training of new firefighters or who have worked together in other fire stations. For some firefighters, participating in these painful memorials would be a torture that has lasted for more than a year, bringing them untold suffering once again.

p12.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p13.original: 在“9·11”事件中，消防员和其他人的反应和经历是人们在应激情境中的典型反应和经历吗？什么因素可以解释人们对应激的生理和心理反应的个体差异呢？
p13.en: Were the reactions and experiences of firefighters and others typical of people's responses and experiences in a passion context during the events of 11 September? What factors explain the individual differences in the physical and psychological responses to stress?

p14.original: 当然，冲进正在倒塌的大楼并不是人们该有的正常反应，而是训练有素的救援人员的习得反应。但是，幸存者感到内疚及世界各地的人在网上和电视上反复收看灾难情境所引起的延迟应激反应，这些是“正常”的应激反应吗？我们可以把这些反应和我们自己的应激反应联系起来吗？在考虑这些问题时，几个相关问题随之而来。
p14.en: Of course, breaking into a falling building is not a normal response that people deserve, but is a trained response by a well-trained rescue worker. But is it “normal” that the guilt of survivors and the delayed stress caused by repeated online and television sightings of disaster situations around the world? Can we link these reactions to our own stress? In considering these issues, several related issues follow.

p15.original: 应激源并不局限于重大的悲剧、创伤和灾难。所有人在日常生活中都会遇到潜在的应激情境，比如在工作中、人际交往中、学校里、交通拥堵时或生病时。但是你有没有注意到，有些人遇到一些很小的烦恼就感到压力很大，而有些人即使在危急关头也表现得镇定自若。此外，有些人能在经历巨大的应激后很快复原，而有些人却久久难以平复。如何解释个体在面对相同应激源时的差异反应？
p15.en: The sources of response are not limited to major tragedies, traumas and disasters. All people experience potential passions in their daily lives, such as at work, in interpersonal relationships, in schools, when traffic is blocked or when they are ill. But have you noticed that some people are under stress when they encounter some minor problems and that some are calm even at a time of crisis? Moreover, some are able to recover quickly after a great deal of stress, while others have been unable to recover for a long time. How can we explain the individual's differential response to the same stressors?

p16.original: 我们还必须考虑应激源在近几个世纪里是如何变化的，以及应激反应是如何在人类几千年的进化中帮助我们生存下来的。当下，许多文化环境里的生活节奏比先辈们的生活节奏更快。我们如今面临的应激与先辈们面临的应激有何不同？生活环境的不同会对应激反应的有效性产生哪些影响？
p16.en: We must also consider how the sources of stress have changed in recent centuries and how the stress has helped us survive thousands of years of human evolution. In many cultural settings, life is at a faster pace than that of its predecessors. What difference does the stress we face today have to do with the stress that our predecessors are facing? What are the impacts of differences in the living environment on the effectiveness of stress?

p17.original: 快节奏文化（如图所示）创造了现代社会独有的环境应激源。
p17.en: A fast-paced culture (as shown in the figure) creates a unique source of environmental stress in modern societies.

p18.original: 享受慢节奏生活的文化不会面临城市居民所经历的那些应激源。
p18.en: A culture that enjoys a slow pace of living does not face the stress that urban dwellers experience.

p20.original: 想要了解人类对应激的反应，多元化视角是必要的。当面对应激时，我们的身体和大脑会发生什么变化？我们的思维过程、先前的学习、人格特征、特定的生命阶段和社会环境是如何调节这些生理反应的（见图14-1）？
p20.en: A pluralist perspective is necessary to understand the human response to the strain. What happens to our bodies and brains when we face stress? How do our mental processes, prior learning, personality characteristics, specific stages of life and social circumstances regulate these biological responses (see figure 14-1)?

p21.original: 通过图14-1探索其中的交互性，你能针对每个视角想出一些例子吗？选择一些流行的建议与你的想法进行比较，并阅读一些其他例子，从多个角度理解应激的复杂本质是必要的。
p21.en: By exploring the interaction in figure 14-1, can you come up with some examples of each perspective? The choice of some popular suggestions is compared to your ideas and some other examples are necessary to understand the complex nature of stress from multiple angles.

p22.original: 我们能在多大程度上控制自己对应激的反应，以及控制应激对我们身心健康的潜在影响呢？好消息是，我们并不总是被近期的应激困扰，为了更有效地应对应激带来的挑战，我们可以做一些改变。因此，我们会以更积极的方式阐述本章的内容，不仅会展示有效的应对策略，还会介绍提升健康水平、韧性和幸福感的新的健康心理学视角。此外，我们还会强调，经常锻炼身体是保障身心健康的最重要的因素。了解应激形成的方式和原因，以及应对应激的最佳方法可以提高我们的生活质量。
p22.en: To what extent can we control our own response to stress and the potential impact of stress on our physical and mental health? The good news is that we are not always plagued by recent stress, and we can make some changes in order to respond more effectively to the challenge posed by stress. We will therefore elaborate on this chapter in a more proactive manner, not only demonstrating effective coping strategies, but also introducing new health psychology perspectives that raise health levels, resilience and well-being. In addition, we would like to emphasize that frequent physical exercise is the most important factor in ensuring physical and mental health. Understanding the ways and causes of stress formation and the best ways to deal with stress can improve our quality of life.

p23.original: 当我们探讨这些问题时，请你回想自己过去及现阶段所面临的应激，并思考本章的内容如何帮助你理解生活中的应激源，如何改善你感知和管理应激的方式。尽管大学生的日常生活应激与消防员和其他救援人员相比要小，但最近寻求心理帮助的大学生不断增多，大学生的自杀率也在不断上升。这迫使我们审视这些学业应激从何而来，以及如何才能更好地应对它。
p23.en: When we look at these issues, please recall the stress you have faced in the past and at this stage, and how the content of this chapter helps you to understand the stress in life and how to improve the way you perceive and manage it. Although the daily stress of university students is smaller than that of firefighters and other rescue workers, the number of university students seeking psychological help has recently increased and the suicide rate among university students is rising. This compels us to look at where these educational stressors come from and how they can be better addressed.
